See the formula ↓

How the calculation works

Grade percentage = Points earned ÷ Points possible × 100

A worked example

Earning 42 points out of 50 gives 42 ÷ 50 × 100 = 84%. If a second assignment earns 18 out of 20, the pooled points percentage is (42 + 18) ÷ (50 + 20) × 100 = 85.71%. Averaging the two percentages would give 87%, a different weighting.

Before you use the result

Decimal points are supported for partial credit. Possible points must be positive and earned points must be between zero and the maximum. This tool does not accept extra-credit scores above the maximum. It also does not apply category weights: a percentage on one assignment is not automatically your overall course grade. Use the weighted calculator when your syllabus assigns separate category percentages.

Results display to two decimal places unless stated otherwise. Read our calculation methodology for scope and limitations.

Frequently asked questions

What letter grade is my percentage?

Use your school’s grading table. The same percentage can correspond to different letter grades in different systems.

Can I enter decimal marks?

Yes. For example, 17.5 out of 20 gives 87.5%.

Is this the same as percent correct?

Only if the points awarded accurately reflect your correct answers. For equal-value questions without partial credit, the test score calculator is quicker.
